dataList.content:
Eventually, the boulder began to roll down again.
最后，石头又一次开始缓缓滚落。

I turned my gaze to Meursault.
我看向默尔索。

His face, screwed up and straining; his cheek, pressed tight against the boulder; his shoulder, beneath the sediment-covered mass; and his leg, braced to support it. At the end of the outstretched arms were his hands, caked with dirt. And there, in Meursault, I saw a certainty that was wholly human.
抽动的表情，紧贴巨石的脸颊，支撑覆满堆积物的石头的肩膀，然后是全力支撑着的那条腿，以及再次接住巨石的臂端，那双沾满泥土的手。从那一切里，我看到了属于人类的确定性。

A human drenched in sweat.
默尔索，他此刻是个大汗淋漓的人类。

<Are you all right, Meursault?>
<没事吧，默尔索？>

The boulder was heavy. The slightest error in balancing it sent it rolling down again.
石头很重，稍微偏离重心便会导致它再次滚落。

<... That must've been a hard punishment to bear.>
<……真是痛苦的刑罚啊。>

... It wasn't a punishment, Manager.
……那并不是刑罚，经理。

I have never once... regarded the act of rolling that boulder... as punishment.
我从未……把推动巨石的行为……当做刑罚。

<But... you were hurting.>
<可是……你很辛苦吧。>

And yet, ironically... within that continuous pain...
不过……矛盾的是……在这份持续不断的痛苦中……

... I found enjoyment.
我却感到了享受。

Yes. When I was going downhill again to retrieve the boulder.
是的。当为了寻找滚落的巨石，折返回头时。

I knew I was bound to return for it, that it would invariably fall again, that it would hurt. But at very occasional moments...
那段明知它必定会落下，明知会痛苦却依旧回头去寻找的时间。偶尔……

I enjoyed it.
让我感到享受。
